data.title: Apple Stocks Rise Although Doubling Macs Adds 47% More Throughput in Muse Test
data.description:
Apple, the device and computing-platform company , faces a practical test for running AI locally: how much extra computing power justifies buying more hardware? Shares traded at $343.795, up approximately 0.53%, after the 9:30 a.m. ET market open on October 16. The question for professional buyers is straightforward. Does adding more Macs deliver enough extra performance to justify the bill?

According to Macworld's analysis, Apple's research measured Muse Spark Open at 24.99 tokens per second on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios, versus 36.73 on four. The benchmark used tensor parallelization, four-bit precision, 8,192 input tokens and 128 generated tokens. Double the computers delivered roughly 47% more throughput. That is a meaningful improvement, but buyers cannot assume performance rises in step with hardware spending.

Faster initial responses could strengthen the case, alongside privacy and the ability to handle demanding workloads locally. Still, one specialized benchmark does not establish a broad Mac sales opportunity. Valuation raises the bar: the $343.795 share price sits 19.1% above the $288.67 GF Value estimate, leaving less room for disappointing execution. Investors need evidence of professional customers buying these configurations repeatedly before treating local AI as a major new hardware growth engine.

data.title: Oil Futures Rise on Middle East, Russia-Ukraine Concerns — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid and Anthony Harrup

Oil prices turned higher Friday as Ukraine renewed attacks on Russian refineries, adding to concerns about persistent Middle East supply risks and uncertainty over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude for December delivery was up 3.2% at $109.28 a barrel, and December West Texas Intermediate gained 2.2% to $98.59 a barrel. Front-month WTI for November was up 2.8% at $100.71 a barrel, topping the $100 mark for the first time in a month.

"The main reason is that Ukraine has renewed its attacks on Russian oil refineries," said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital. "Despite the IEA and its member countries having already released approximately 300 million barrels from emergency oil reserves, with another 100 million barrels likely to be released, prices continue to rise."

The International Energy Agency said Thursday that its members agreed to accelerate the release of around 100 million barrels of previously pledged emergency oil stocks, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel to be released as soon as possible.

About 330 million barrels have already been released, and the agency said total releases would exceed the 400 million barrels initially agreed upon in March, with some members contributing additional volumes.

"We're still in a bull market," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of trading at BOK Financial. Flows through the Strait of Hormuz aren't reliable, expectations of Russian diesel coming onto the market aren't being met, and with Ukrainian attacks on refineries "those barrels are going to have trouble getting to the market," he said.

A third factor is that demand destruction "at least in the U.S. is not happening," he added.

Despite recovering Middle East oil flows, uncertainty surrounding the conflict continues to support crude prices, analysts at ING said. The bank said a sustained recovery in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz could gradually reduce the geopolitical risk premium, but a U.S.-Iran agreement would be needed to give markets greater confidence that higher flows could be maintained.

However, oil prices above $100 a barrel appear increasingly stretched relative to market fundamentals, according to Norbert Rucker, head of economics and next generation research at Julius Baer. Middle Eastern exports have largely recovered and global inventories remain comfortable, while geopolitical risk premiums and elevated freight costs could ease, he said.

"The relative calm in oil markets seems untenable, as the gradual recovery in Middle East oil flows has come under pressure of late from a resurgence of attacks on shipping," Barclays analyst Amarpreet Singh said in a note. "What looked like a tail risk scenario a few weeks ago--in which a diplomatic resolution takes us back to pre-war levels of Middle East supply and spare capacity--looks an even more remote possibility at this point," he added.

Shipping risks remain high after two cargo ships sank near the Strait of Hormuz following attacks, The Wall Street Journal reported. U.K. Maritime Trade Operations separately reported Wednesday that two container ships were struck by unidentified projectiles while transiting the waterway.

Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com and Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: Irish public sector trade unions suspend second day of strikes
data.description:
Irish public sector trade unions suspended a second day of widespread strikes planned for next week after they agreed on Friday to begin mediated discussions with the government this weekend on the terms for new pay talks.

Much of Ireland's public sector including teachers, health workers and civil servants on Wednesday staged the country's first major strike in almost two decades after failing for months to agree with ministers on the basis for negotiations on pay rises.

The two sides agreed on Friday to begin a process aimed at finding a basis for formal negotiations to commence.

"I believe that there is now a prospect of progress in the process that has been established. Obviously we will need to see the government's words backed up in practice," Kevin Callinan, chair of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions public services committee, told national broadcaster RTE.

data.title: BIRK Stock Downgraded By Williams Trading – Firm Believes ‘Lack Of Compelling New Product’ Is Affecting Demand
data.description:
Key points:
  • Williams Trading said sell-through rates are slowing in the Americas, while EMEA faces a disconnect between sell-in and sell-through, most evident at Zalando, according to Investing.com.
  • The firm said a “lack of compelling new product” is beginning to prompt wholesale partners in the Americas to pull back, according to The Fly.
  • Raymond James lowered its price target to $42 from $52 but maintained ‘Outperform’, citing DTC growth, EMEA performance, wholesale orders and product diversification.

Birkenstock (BIRK) shares were in focus on Friday after Williams Trading and Raymond James lowered their price targets on the stock.

According to The Fly, Williams Trading cut its price target to $27 from $39 and downgraded Birkenstock to ‘Sell’ from ‘Hold,’ saying the company’s fiscal 2028 targets will not be met. Raymond James lowered its target to $42 from $52 but maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating.

BIRK stock traded 4.3% lower at the time of writing.

Williams Trading Flags Promotional Activity, Wholesale Caution

According to The Fly, Williams Trading said Birkenstock’s fiscal 2028 targets will not be met. The firm noted that promotional activity is increasing, especially in Europe, and many of the company’s most loyal wholesale accounts in the Americas are adopting a more tempered approach to their 2027 plans.

Williams Trading also said a “lack of compelling new product” is beginning to cause wholesalers to step back in the Americas, The Fly reported.

Separately, according to a report published by Investing.com, Williams Trading said sell-through rates are decelerating in the Americas, although the market remains clean. In EMEA, the firm said there is a disconnect between sell-in and sell-through, most evident at Zalando.

Williams Trading noted it would not be surprised if Birkenstock tempers its fiscal 2028 targets when fourth-quarter earnings are announced later next month. Birkenstock’s fiscal 2028 outlook calls for revenue of €3.02 billion ($3.40 billion) to €3.183 billion ($3.58 billion) and a three-year constant-currency revenue CAGR of 13% to 15%, according to the report.

Raymond James Cites Growth And Product Diversification

Raymond James cited accelerating direct-to-consumer (DTC) growth, strong EMEA performance, healthy wholesale orders and product diversification as factors supporting Birkenstock’s fourth-quarter guidance and fiscal 2027 EPS of €2.53, according to The Fly.

The firm said the earnings per share (EPS) forecast represents 28% year-over-year growth and is above consensus. Store expansion, e-commerce improvements and lower tariffs were also cited as drivers of potential upside.

Retail View On BIRK

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment toward Birkenstock remained ‘Bearish’, while message volume was ‘Normal’ over the past 24 hours.

BIRK shares have dropped over 18% year-to-date.

(Exchange Rate: €1 = $1.13)

data.title: European Equities Close Higher On AI Optimism
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - European stocks closed broadly higher on Friday with stocks from several sectors finding fairly good support ahead of quarterly earnings updates due from early next week. Although higher oil prices weighed a bit, easing concerns about interest rates and AI-related investments rendered the mood positive.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's comments defending the financial health of AI computing supplier CoreWeave Inc. aided sentiment.

Defense stocks found support as European leaders gathered in Brussels to reaffirm their support for President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.amidst the escalating conflict in Ukraine.

The pan European Stoxx 600 climbed 0.72%. The UK's FTSE 100 gained 0.38%, Germany's DAX jumped 0.95% and France's CAC 40 ended 0.28% up. Switzerland's SMI settled with a gain of 0.29%. FTSE 100, DAX and CAC 40 all posted gains for the week.

Among other markets in Europe, Austria, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Greece, Iceland, Ireland, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Russia, Spain and Sweden closed higher.

The Russian market declined sharply, while Belgium edged down marginally.

In the UK market, Babcock International climbed 3.6%. WPP, Kingfisher, Weir, BAE Systems, AutoTrader Group, Metlen Energy & Metals, British American Tobacco and National Grid gained 2%-3.1%.

Ithaca Energy gained more than 1%. The British oil and gas firm announced that its Chief Executive Officer, Luciano Vasques is set to retire by March 31, 2027.

Balfour Beatty, Diageo, Intercontinental Hotels Group, Imperial Brands, Fresnillo, Endeavour Mining, Reckitt Benckiser, Standard Life, JD Sports Fashion and Pearson rallied 1.5%-2%.

Scottish Mortgage dropped 3.1%. AstraZeneca and Polar Technology Trust ended down 2% and 1.8%, respectively. Natwest Group, British Land, Computacenter, Segro and The Sage Group closed lower by 1%-1.2%.

In the German market, Rheinmetall rallied more than 6.5%. BMW moved up 3.5%. Mercedes-Benz, Fresenius and Volkswagen gained 2.7%-3%.

Siemens Energy, RWE, E.ON, Daimler Truck Holding, Porsche Automobil Holding, Heidelberg Materials, Zalando, Henkel, Siemens Healthineers, Deutsche Boerse, Scout24, Deutsche Telekom, BASF, Hochtief and Allianz moved up 1%-2%.

Shares of sports car manufacturer Porsche moved higher after the group unveiled the Mission S vision model, showcasing the future evolution of its design identity under the 'Sportswagenschmiede '35' strategy.

SAP drifted down by about 1%. Continental, Qiagen and Infineon declined marginally.

In the French market, EssilorLuxottica surged nearly 4%. Renault moved up 3.3%. Thales, Stellantis, Pernod Ricard, Airbus, Edenred, Accor and Bouygues gained 1.4%-3%.

Teleperformance shed about 2.2%. Schneider Electric closed lower by 1.8%. Publicis Groupe, Michelin and Eurofins Scientific lost 1.1%-1.25%.

In economic news, The euro area trade balance showed a shortfall of EUR 16.1 billion in August, compared with a surplus of EUR 10.7 billion posted in July. In the same period last year, the deficit was EUR 1.7 billion.

Exports of goods increased 9.9% from a year ago, which was faster than the 8.8% rise in July. At the same time, growth in imports accelerated sharply to 16.7% from 9.1%.

Eurozone inflation rose to 3.8% in September, marking the highest since September 2023, from 3.2% in August. The rate matched the flash estimate published on October 2.

Excluding energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, core inflation rose slightly to 2.5%, as estimated, from 2.4% in the previous month.

Month-on-month, the harmonized index of consumer prices gained 0.6%, matching the initial estimate.

data.title: IBM Q3 Earnings Preview: What To Expect From Upcoming Report
data.description:
International Business Machines heads into its Oct. 21 earnings report with investors looking for evidence that its artificial intelligence and software businesses can sustain growth amid intensifying competition across the technology sector.

Analysts expect third-quarter earnings of $2.86 per share on revenue of $16.81 billion. The results will give investors a fresh look at IBM's growth trajectory and its ability to meet Wall Street's expectations.

Software performance, particularly at Red Hat, will be an important area to watch. Stronger growth could help support overall results, while investors will also look for signs that demand for consulting services is stabilizing. Management's outlook may prove just as important as the quarterly figures.

IBM's AI strategy remains another key consideration. Investors will want to see whether customer demand for AI products and services is translating into revenue growth and creating additional opportunities across its business.

The main risk is that IBM delivers results close to expectations but provides a weaker outlook for the coming quarters. With options traders pricing in a potential post-earnings move of nearly 8%, the report could trigger a sharp share-price reaction in either direction.

data.title: Clients Are Cheating on Their Financial Advisors. With AI. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kenneth Corbin

For all the talk about the potential for artificial intelligence to replace financial advisors, a new survey suggests an alternative scenario — that clients will use AI as a second opinion. Americans who use an advisor are far more likely to consult AI for financial advice than those who don't, according to the poll, fielded by Evergreen.ai, an AI-powered financial advice and planning app.

In a recent poll of nearly 2,000 Americans, Evergreen found that almost 64% of those who have a financial advisor said that they have asked AI about money issues. Among respondents who don't use a human advisor, that figure dropped to 38.5%.

Among all survey participants, 48.4% said that they have asked an AI chatbot about their finances in the past year. Of those who did, nearly 78% said they acted on the response they received.

"Americans are desperately seeking financial guidance," says Evergreen founder and CEO Bill Harris. "They are looking for answers wherever they can find them."

The survey showed that some respondents are using AI independently from their advisor. The participants with an advisor were far more likely to act on an AI-generated recommendation without researching it than those without an advisor. Evergreen concludes that "rather than replacing professional advice, AI appears to be layering on top of it, often without the same scrutiny."

That finding could be a product of so-called hybrid clients, those who work with an advisor who oversees a managed account while also maintaining a separate, self-directed account.

The survey also uncovered some familiar patterns, such as the lower confidence reported by respondents without an advisor compared with those who work with a financial professional.

Retirement uncertainty. Respondents indicated uncertainty around retirement planning and hesitancy to make major financial decisions. More than 42% of survey participants said that they had never bothered to estimate how much money they will need for retirement. Of those, nearly one-third said they expect to retire within 15 years.

Almost 90% of respondents said that they had put off at least one financial matter longer than they should have in the past year, with more than half saying they don't know where to start or that they have difficulty understanding their options.

"People are making decisions about taxes, retirement, and their financial futures without always having the answers they need," Harris says. "A human advisor remains invaluable, especially for complex decisions, and more people deserve access to clear information along the way."

data.title: Microsoft is the only hyperscaler not forecast to dip into negative FCF in the next year
data.description:
Microsoft stands alone among major hyperscalers as the only one not forecast to dip into negative free cash flow territory over the next twelve months, according to BofA Global Research Equity and Quant Strategy.

Amazon , Alphabet , , Oracle , and Meta are all expected to fall into negative free cash flow by 2027, with BofA Global Research projecting these hyperscalers' next-twelve-month free cash flow estimates will drop below negative $25,000 between 2026 and 2028.

The outlook isn't entirely bleak for the sector, according to BofA Global Research, which expects hyperscalers' free cash flow to shift from negative to positive by the second half of 2027 as AI-related revenue growth accelerates and AI capital expenditures decelerate.

However, the research firm warns of significant risk: AI capex has surprised to the upside by a much wider margin than revenue—50% versus 20% this year—meaning 2027 expectations imply a marked shift in trend.

BofA Global Research's estimated compute demand through 2030 implies approximately $10T of spend, roughly $2T above current forecasts.

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq set for steep weekly losses as AI jitters rattle investors
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes down: Dow 0.03%, S&P 0.56%, Nasdaq 1.3%
  • Chips, neocloud companies slide as debt concerns linger
  • Gains in banks limit Dow's fall, set for weekly gains

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Purvi Agarwal

The benchmark S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end the week in the red, with technology stocks coming under more pressure on Friday over cracks in the AI trade and adding to losses.

The S&P 500 information technology index fell 1.5% and was the biggest drag. Nvidia-backed CoreWeave slid 10.3% on lingering debt concerns. The data centre operator's bonds sold off sharply this week, pushing yields to above 15%.

Semiconductors bore the brunt of the selloff, with the broader chips index dropping 1.8% — set for its steepest eight-session percentage decline since the "Liberation Day" selloff in April 2025.

Most megacap stocks tumbled and brought the Nasdaq close to a one-month low. Meta slipped 2.3% and Microsoft lost 1.8%.

AI stocks have cratered this week over concerns that data centre operators might not turn profitable in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise. Worries over rising competition from China also dented sentiment.

"When investors start worrying that AI names are overvalued, they gravitate toward lower-multiple stocks with stable cash flows," said Dennis Dick, founder and market structure analyst at Triple D Trading.

Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors are weighing a lower valuation for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

At 12:19 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 14.74 points, or 0.03%, to 52,162.95, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 43.53 points, or 0.56%, to 7,700.38 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 348.31 points, or 1.30%, to 26,364.72.

Most other S&P 500 sectors rose. The energy index was the biggest percentage gainer, up 1.5%, while the financials index rose 1%.

Gains in Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase lifted the Dow to its highest level in over a month. The index is set for a weekly advance, with investors rushing to defensive sectors such as healthcare and consumer staples.

"What we're seeing now is money rotating out of a very crowded AI trade and into value names," Dick added.

The S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since early June, faced with an AI-led rout, mixed bank earnings and inflation data. The Nasdaq eyed its sharpest weekly fall since June 22.

Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week have confirmed that price pressures are extending beyond energy products.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh also said a spending surge was boosting inflation, but added that the US economy remained resilient and benefited from the AI-driven investment boom.

Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays now expects 25 basis point hikes each in December and January.

Meanwhile, Tesla failed to hold on to gains from before the bell — as much as 3% — after unveiling a redesigned Roadster, powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX.

Netflix appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares were down 2.6%.

Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.94-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week highs and no new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 46 new highs and 200 new lows.

data.title: Micron Stocks Fall 3.5% Although Bullish Memory Commentary Meets a Cash Test
data.description:
Micron Technology, the memory and storage-chip producer , faces tougher questions about the durability of its memory boom, with shares at $898.77, down 3.5%, around 10:34 a.m. ET on October 16. According to Benzinga, Bernstein analyst Mark Newman sees value in memory stocks after their retreat, even as price increases lose momentum. Slower increases do not mean prices are falling. They do put more pressure on earnings growth to justify the investment story.

Micron's September 30 earnings release reported quarterly revenue of $54.229 billion and adjusted free cash flow of $33.199 billion. That is roughly 61.2 cents of adjusted free cash flow for every revenue dollar. Management's next-quarter sales forecast stands at $61.5 billion, plus or minus $1.5 billion. The midpoint implies another 13.4% sequential increase. Cash gives Micron room to expand. Earning attractive returns on that expansion is the next test.

The valuation snapshot shows shares trading 14.63% above GF Value of $784.03, suggesting the pullback has not erased the premium to that estimate. Investors still need to weigh that premium against future growth. The Stock Analysis overview provides additional financial context, but the operating numbers deserve the closest watch: revenue, margins and capital spending. Strong cash generation can fund more production. Sustained demand and disciplined spending will determine whether that production creates lasting shareholder value.

data.title: Novartis ends mid-stage Fabhalta trial targeting serious kidney condition
data.description:
Swiss drugmaker Novartis has terminated a mid-stage study testing its drug Fabhalta in patients with a serious kidney condition, citing "strategic considerations", according to a federal clinical trials registry.

  • The trial was evaluating whether the oral medication was safe and effective for treating lupus nephritis when added to standard medical care

  • Lupus nephritis is a severe inflammation of the kidneys caused by the autoimmune disease lupus

  • The government database, last updated on October 15, shows Novartis decided to conclude the study after completing the first part

  • It gives no other explanation and does not say whether safety or effectiveness played a role

  • Endpoints News reported the development earlier on Friday

  • Novartis did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment

  • The US FDA first approved Fabhalta in 2023 for a rare blood disorder called PNH. It has since been approved for two kidney diseases, IgA nephropathy and C3 glomerulopathy

data.title: Chandrasekaran, P.B. Balaji to join Iveco board as Tata deal reaches final stage
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- New Delhi: Tata Sons' chairperson Natarajan Chandrasekaran, Jaguar Land Rover's chief executive P.B. Balaji, and Tata Motors' managing director Girish Wagh are among the top executives set to join Iveco's board if Tata Motors' acquisition of the Italian truckmaker clears its final hurdles.

The deal was approved by Iveco shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on Friday, with attention now turning to Tata securing 80% acceptance of the tender offer by 26 October.

The appointments are conditional on the deal going through. While Chandrasekaran will join as Iveco's chairperson, Balaji and Wagh will join as non-independent directors. Iveco had proposed a six-member board following the completion of the deal, with Olof Persson continuing as CEO and two independent directors also joining the board, showed Iveco's filings.

The new board members will serve until the end of Iveco's annual general meeting in 2027. Chandrasekaran, Balaji and Wagh, along with CEO Olof Persson, have been proposed for terms running up to the 2027 AGM, while the two independent directors will serve for two years from the completion of the deal.

Tata Motors' tender offer has so far received acceptances for 28.4% of Iveco's shares, according to the latest update, with Tata raising its offer to €14.40 per share on 9 October, calling it its best and final offer.

Since the price increase, the subscription rate hasn't moved much, with 10 days remaining before the deal's deadline to reach the 80% threshold.

"Shareholders approved all the resolutions proposed by the board of directors," Iveco said in a statement on Friday. The company also said the approval meant "the minimum acceptance level of the offer will be reduced from 95% to 80% of the common shares."

The EGM approval was important for Tata Motors, as it removed one of the key hurdles for the transaction and lowered the acceptance threshold from 95% to 80%. The resolutions approved by shareholders include those related to the proposed board, post-offer restructuring and changes to Iveco's voting structure. The appointments of the new board members will take effect after the settlement of the offer.

The focus now shifts to shareholder participation in the tender offer. Iveco's largest shareholder Exor, which owns about 27.06% of the company's common shares, has already tendered its stake.

The remaining large institutional shareholders are being closely watched as the offer heads towards its 26 October deadline. Hedge funds Davidson Kempner and Syquant Capital and activist investor Petrus Advisers together hold about 20.4% of Iveco's common shares. None of the three had tendered their shares so far.

Petrus had opposed Tata Motors' original €14.10 offer on 29 September, arguing that it undervalued Iveco and did not give shareholders an adequate share of the value expected from the combination. Tata subsequently raised the offer by about 2% to €14.40 per share on 9 October, citing delays in obtaining regulatory approvals. The company said the revised price would not be increased further.

The acquisition was first announced in July 2025, when Tata Motors agreed to acquire Iveco's commercial vehicle business for about €3.8 billion. The transaction excluded Iveco's defence business, which was subsequently sold to Italian defence company Leonardo for an enterprise value of €1.7 billion.

The combined business would have annual revenue of about €21 billion ( Rs.2.28 trillion) and sales of more than 590,000 vehicles, according to the September 2026 offer documents from Tata Motors and Iveco.

Tata Motors' revised €14.40 offer would value the common shares at about €3.91 billion if all 271.2 million shares covered by the offer are tendered. The offer is being made through TML CV Holdings B.V., an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Motors.

For Tata Motors, the deal would expand its presence in Europe and other international markets and add Iveco's established product portfolio and manufacturing footprint.

If Tata reaches the 80% acceptance threshold, it can move ahead with the post-offer restructuring approved by Iveco shareholders. The plans include a demerger and share sale, and, depending on the level of ownership achieved, steps towards delisting Iveco from Euronext Milan.

data.title: Rs.2 per share dividend stock: Do you own this real estate stock? Check record date to qualify for cash reward
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- Real estate developer Oberoi Realty announced a reward for shareholders by declaring a second interim dividend of Rs.2 per share for FY27, alongside its financial results for the September quarter on Friday, October 16.

The company also fixed Friday, October 23, as the record date to determine shareholders' eligibility for the dividend payment. The dividend payment will commence on October 30, 2026, for eligible shareholders.

"This is to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on October 16, 2026, has declared the second interim dividend for FY27 at the rate of Rs.2 (Rupees Two only) per equity share, i.e., 20% of the face value of equity shares of Rs.10 each," the company said in its regulatory filing.

Investors looking to benefit from the payout must ensure they purchase the stock in time to be eligible for the dividend. Under India's T+1 settlement cycle, shares purchased on or after the record date will not qualify for the dividend.

Oberoi Realty follows a quarterly dividend payout policy, distributing a portion of its profits to shareholders and offering them an opportunity to earn regular income alongside potential capital appreciation.

For the September quarter (Q2FY27), the company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs.761.65 crore, a marginal increase from Rs.760.26 crore in the year-ago period.

Total income fell 6% to Rs.1,736.37 crore during the second quarter of FY27 from Rs.1,844.84 crore in the corresponding period of the preceding fiscal, according to a regulatory filing.

The company's expenses declined to Rs.744.94 crore from Rs.863.35 crore, helping it register marginal profit growth during the July-September quarter of FY27.

During the first half of FY27, the company's net profit rose to Rs.1,305.16 crore from Rs.1,181.51 crore in the year-ago period. Total income increased to Rs.3,098.06 crore from Rs.2,918.82 crore.

Mumbai-based Oberoi Realty is one of India's leading real estate developers, primarily focusing on the development of luxury homes.

data.title: Stablecoin remittances cost 84% less than traditional transfers, report finds
data.description:
Stablecoin-funded remittances continue to offer substantial cost savings over traditional money transfers, particularly in emerging markets, reinforcing one of the leading use cases for digital dollars as payment activity grows.

According to a new third-quarter report from Borderless.xyz, a stablecoin payments network, sending a $200 remittance through stablecoin-funded payment rails costs a median of 1%, or $2, compared with 6.36%, or $12.72, for traditional remittances, based on World Bank data.

The difference makes stablecoin-funded remittances roughly 84% cheaper, although the comparison uses Borderless’s third-quarter 2026 pricing and World Bank figures from the same period in 2025.

The savings are also substantial across emerging markets. In Sub-Saharan Africa, stablecoin-funded remittances cost 2.9%, compared with 8.46% for traditional transfers. In Latin America, the costs are 1.25% and 5.64%, respectively.

Business payments made through stablecoins are also significantly cheaper, according to the report. A $10,000 stablecoin-funded transfer to the eurozone costs as little as $26 when routed through the lowest-cost provider, compared with $52 across all corridors at the median provider.

By comparison, a traditional international bank wire costs between $135 and $150 for the same amount, including transfer fees and an assumed 1% foreign-exchange margin.

Stablecoins offer significant cost savings on larger business transactions. Source: Borderless.xyz

Stablecoin payouts settle in minutes, but reliability varies

Beyond cost savings, the Borderless report found that stablecoin-funded payments can reach recipients’ local bank accounts in minutes, depending on the payment network used.

In Brazil, payouts through the PIX network settled in a median of two minutes during the third quarter, while Mexico’s SPEI network took three minutes. Colombia’s PSE network also recorded a median settlement time of two minutes.

By comparison, traditional SWIFT transfers typically settled the next business day, with the slowest 10% taking three business days.

However, payment completion rates varied considerably. Mexico’s SPEI network successfully completed 98.6% of payouts, followed by Brazil’s PIX at 97.8%. Colombia’s PSE network completed 79%, while Costa Rica’s SINPE recorded a completion rate of just 73%.

The findings come as stablecoin transaction activity continues to grow. Standard Chartered recently highlighted rising transaction volumes despite relatively flat growth in the overall stablecoin market capitalization this year. The bank expects the market to reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than its previous forecast.

data.title: Tesla Stocks Rise Although Roadster Reveal Leaves Pricing and Volume Unset
data.description:
Tesla, the electric-vehicle and energy-storage manufacturer , faces a long wait for Roadster revenue, with shares at $364.47, up approximately 0.56%, at 10:58 a.m. ET on October 16. According to The Fly, JPMorgan maintained its Neutral rating and pointed to a 2028 production target. Final pricing and planned production volumes remain undisclosed, leaving investors without the inputs needed to estimate the car's sales contribution.

The immediate earnings story runs through products already selling. Tesla's October 2 operating update reported 486,532 quarterly vehicle deliveries, including 478,237 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, alongside 13.7 gigawatt-hours of energy-storage deployments. Those two vehicle models accounted for roughly 98.3% of deliveries. Their margins, together with storage profitability and cash generation, give investors concrete numbers to scrutinize when third-quarter financial results arrive after the October 21 market close.

Valuation adds another hurdle. The chart places the share price 8.38% above the GF Value estimate of $336.28, suggesting the stock already carries a premium to that benchmark. The market snapshot provides additional trading context, but the next financial test is straightforward: whether Tesla's existing businesses can produce earnings that support its valuation while investors wait for the Roadster.

data.title: RNAi drug developer City climbs after upsized IPO
data.description:
City Therapeutics , a developer of a novel treatment class known as RNA interference therapies, added more than 20% on Friday after an upsized initial public offering that raised roughly $200M in gross proceeds.

Shares of the Cambridge, Massachusetts-based biotech opened for trading at $23 shortly before 12 pm ET, implying a 28% gain from the IPO price. The stock gradually lost its initial momentum, slipping ~5% to approach $21.93 about an hour later, still implying a 23% jump.

Late Thursday, the company priced the offering of more than 11.1M of its shares at $18 apiece, with underwriters having a 30-day option to buy up to 1.7M shares additionally at the IPO price less discounts and commissions.

City , co-founded by John Maraganore, a former CEO of Alnylam , has a valuation of more than $1.1B based on its latest stock price and the shares of its common stock expected to be outstanding after the offering.

data.title: CoreWeave Stocks Drop 6.84% Despite Cantor's $176 Price Target
data.description:
CoreWeave, the specialized AI-cloud provider , faces a tough test of its bullish investment case, with shares at $64.92, down 6.84%, at 10:35 a.m. ET on October 16. Cantor Fitzgerald sees a buying opportunity. Investors still need proof that the company can turn its enormous construction pipeline into revenue without letting financing costs swallow the rewards.

According to The Fly, Cantor analyst Brett Knoblauch retained an Overweight rating and $176 price target. CoreWeave's August 11 earnings release puts the execution challenge into focus: active power reached approximately 1.5 gigawatts at June-end, against roughly 3.7 gigawatts contracted. Revenue backlog stood at approximately $104 billion, but recognizing that revenue depends on delivering capacity and meeting service requirements. Signed business gives visibility. It does not pay construction bills today.

Active power therefore represented about 40.5% of contracted capacity, leaving a 2.2-gigawatt gap at that reporting date. That is a development pipeline, with spending and execution still ahead. The valuation snapshot adds another caution: a GF Score of 8/100 alongside loss-making earnings highlights weak measured fundamentals despite the huge backlog. The next test is straightforward: bring capacity online, collect customer payments and show that the returns justify the financing burden.

data.title: SK Hynix Stocks Rise With 30% Efficiency Claim in New Memory
data.description:
SK hynix, the memory-chip and AI-server component supplier , presents another way to sell memory into AI infrastructure: shared capacity across servers. Its Korean shares closed at ?1,272,000, up 0.79% on October 16. The pitch goes beyond high-bandwidth memory. More types of memory inside each AI installation could give the company more products to sell.

In its October 16 disclosure, SK hynix described a 256-gigabyte CXL 3.2 module delivering 80 gigabytes per second of bandwidth, with roughly 30% better energy efficiency than its predecessor, according to the company. It also outlined proof-of-concept work with NAVER Cloud to share cached AI data. That is a technical milestone. It does not establish a volume order, a shipment schedule or a revenue contribution.

The GF Score of 76/100 shows strong growth, profitability and financial strength readings, alongside a sharply weaker momentum reading. That gives investors useful context, but it does not settle the commercial question. A successful demonstration still needs to turn into customer qualifications and paying orders. Shared memory could help customers squeeze more work from their servers; the payoff for SK hynix depends on how many modules they buy and the margins those sales deliver.

data.title: TSMC Stocks Fall Although $670 Target Raises the Advanced-Chip Stakes
data.description:
TSMC, the contract chip manufacturer , confronts a higher bar for its AI expansion after Barclays reportedly lifted its price target from $665 to $670 and maintained Overweight. Shares traded at $414.95, down approximately 1.73%, at about 10.25 a.m. ET on October 16. The opportunity is clear: more revenue from its most advanced manufacturing processes. The catch is that cutting-edge production does not automatically translate into AI sales or stronger profits.

The manufacturing mix shows how quickly the business is shifting. Two-nanometer products contributed 8% of third-quarter wafer revenue, while three-nanometer products supplied 33%, according to the earnings-call transcript published October 15. Together, those processes generated 41% of wafer revenue. Seven-nanometer technology and finer accounted for 79%. Meanwhile, Reuters reported that management forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, putting another substantial quarter on the table.

The valuation graphic shows shares trading 14.25% above the $363.20 GF Value estimate, suggesting investors already pay a premium for that growth. That estimate is a valuation reference, not a guaranteed destination. The next test is execution: expand advanced production, maintain yields and keep ramp costs under control. Watch margins alongside the node mix. More leading-edge revenue strengthens the earnings opportunity, but the profit left after expansion costs determines the payoff for shareholders.

data.title: CDC reports 4,410 measles cases as outbreak grows
data.description:
The US CDC on Friday reported 4,410 measles cases nationwide as of October 15, an increase of 330 from its last update a week ago, as an outbreak of the highly contagious disease continues.

Here are key details:

  • Measles-related hospitalizations this year stand at 451, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said

  • The state of Pennsylvania has reported five measles-related deaths

  • The CDC has confirmed two measles-associated deaths in 2026, though it has not identified the states involved

  • Pennsylvania has reported 1,260 measles cases this year as of October 16, with 238 disease-related hospitalizations, according to state health department data

  • Last month, the CDC shifted to using mortality data from the National Center for Health Statistics for measles-related deaths, rather than relying on state health departments, a change that has drawn scrutiny

  • The CDC said on Tuesday it would deploy more support to Pennsylvania to help investigate the outbreak

  • Children and teenagers aged 5 to 19 were the largest group affected by the disease at 1,856, or 42% of cases, followed by adults aged 20 and older at 1,787 cases, or 41%, CDC data showed

  • Earlier this month, the state of New York declared a disaster emergency for the measles outbreak, the first such declaration by a US state

data.title: The NBA bans certain types of parlay bets with its sportsbook partners
data.description:
The NBA sent a memo to partner sportsbooks prohibiting certain types of bets this season. The league has the authority to restrict betting types through its agreements. Going forward, bettors will not be able to include the under on the same player's statistics in parlays. The league also directed sportsbooks to not offer bets on the winner of the opening tip, players to miss specific shots, and under bets on players who are expected to play fewer than 12 minutes in a specific game.

"There's a balance between ensuring that we are removing problematic bet types but also ensuring that we don't just move activity into the illegal market," NBA executive vice president Scott Kaufman-Ross told ESPN. The league thinks the new restrictions strike the right balance.

The NBA has seen a few players wrapped up in betting legal cases. Jontay Porter, formerly of the Toronto Raptors, pleaded guilty in July 2024 to conspiracy to commit wire fraud. He admitted deliberately leaving games early to help bettors win wagers that his statistics would fall below sportsbook thresholds. The NBA banned him for life. Terry Rozier was charged in October 2025 with wire fraud and money laundering conspiracies. Prosecutors allege he tipped off associates that he would exit a March 2023 game early, enabling more than $200K in “under” bets. He has pleaded not guilty.

The impact is negative for DraftKings and FanDuel since parlay bets have higher margins or hold rates that traditional sports bets. DraftKings was down 1.1% in afternoon trading, while FanDuel owner Flutter Entertainment was up 0.1%.
